text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- The government will continue to subsidise the farming sector, Agriculture Minister Dinu Gavrilescu says in an interview.
- Parliament has postponed debates on a bill giving foreigners the right to buy land.
- The farming sector needs strong financial support to get good crops in 1997, the paper said.
- Bankcoop SA remains a safe bank despite allegations saying the bank had given credits which cannot be recovered, bank president Alexandru Dinulescu says in interview.
- Compensations for recent price hikes will amount to some 75 percent, the Labour Ministry says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Some 22 trillion lei are held in arrears by 633 companies which form the hardcore of the financial bottlenecks affecting the economy, the paper says.
- The government resumed talks with trade unions and employers on social protection measures.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Continuous depreciation of the leu currency generates losses for Petrom RA oil company amounting to 9.0 billion lei a day, the paper says.
- Subsidies given to the mining sector in 1997 will be 30 percent lower than last year.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- State-run airline Tarom SA plans to form a joint venture with Air BP to upgrade aircraft fuelling facilities on Bucharest's airports.
- Former ruling Party of Social Democracy asked parliament to discuss in a special session the negotiations currently held by the government with international lenders.
- The government will present trade unions a "black list" of companies due to fire a significant part of their staff.
General
ADEVARUL
- Romania's ex-king Michael could return to his native land without problems provided he observes the country's constitution, National Peasant Party secretary general Radu Vasile is quoted as saying.
- Romanian authorities should not ignore the past and should not forget about the 1939 Nazi-Soviet pact, under which Romania lost land, when negotiating the basic treaty with Ukraine, the paper says.
- Interior Minister Gavril Dejeu threatened to ban a rally planned by miners in Bucharest to protest against the arrest of their leader Miron Cosma. ($=5,969 lei)
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
